> ### Provenance limits that apply to the rows below
>
> - **§2 prints `—/—/—` for six builds** — `advunlearn_{official,parachute,tench,vangogh,garbage_truck}`
>   and `base_sd14` — because their source `gen_*.json` records have `unet: null` **and**

>   0.1333, garbage_truck 0.1333, van_gogh 0.4667) whose identity was never written down; only
>   `base_sd14` is genuinely the base. The dashes are therefore **correct, not missing data**: the
>   numbers exist but are not attributable to an identified checkpoint. They are retained as
>   historical results.
> - **§1's `h63_church_a0.3` and `h63_van_gogh_a0.3` rows are the exception** — they carry 9 attacks
>   each and max H 1.0000 against builds whose `target` is unrecorded and whose checkpoints are
>   `ABSENT`. These are the only table rows that attribute *numbers* to a provenance-gap build.
> - **234 of 335 builds have `ABSENT` checkpoints** (94 `PRESENT`, 7 with no checkpoint field), so
>   roughly **70%** of the corpus is not weight-verifiable. §2 does not mark this per row.
> - **Every `max H (valid)` column inherits the gate bias `FINDING72` measured** — the validity
>   gate's exclusion rate is non-monotone in `T_before` (n = 520), so max-over-valid is computed
>   over a sample whose filtering correlates with how well-erased the arm is.
> - **Base utility is 1.000 on all twelve DEV concepts**, independently confirmed from both
>   `gen_base_sd14.json` and `gen_E6cal_BASE_sd14_on_DEV.json`. That is the control denominator. It
>   establishes that the scorer behaves correctly on **undamaged base outputs**; it does **not**
>   establish its validity on damaged or unusual outputs, where a closed-set 12-way argmax with no
>   reject option can score a degraded model as perfectly generating one surviving label (`D-030`).
> - **Several `max H (valid)` and utility figures below come from arms whose closed-set panel
>   collapsed.** "Retain accuracy collapsed to N/120 under the closed-set scorer" is what those rows
>   support; "the model is destroyed" is not, and no saved images or independent quality assessment
>   exist for any of them (`D-030`, `D-034`).
> - **DUPLICATE CELLS — figures corrected, and the concentration disclosed (`D-025`, `D-051`).** The
>   previous revision said "thirty cells disagree by up to **8/15** images". Both halves are
>   superseded. Within the 696 indexed records: **68 duplicate `(arm, seed, lr, steps)` cells over
>   178 rows**, of which **29 disagree on `H_after`** (30 including `gate_valid`), at a **maximum
>   spread of 0.7333 = 11 of 15 images**. `0.5333 = 8/15` is the **strict-key subset only** and was
>   wrongly made the headline. Over all 808 records: 74 cells across 224 files, 33 disagreeing.
>   **No attack record carries a code-version field**, and `run_inventory.json.code_commit` is `null`
>   for all 234 entries, so the disagreements **cannot be adjudicated from the records at all**.
>
>   **AND THE PART NOBODY HAD STATED: all 29 disagreeing cells belong to the single arm
>   `BASE(unmodified)`** — the attack-on-base control. This cuts both ways and both halves are
>   recorded here. It **reduces** the concern, because the disagreement is concentrated in the
>   unmodified-base control rather than spread through the defence arms, so it does **not** undermine
>   the defence-arm comparisons. It is still **unexplained** — an unmodified base attacked twice
>   should not diverge by 11/15 images.
>
>   **Which rows below inherit it, named explicitly:** the **15 `BASE(unmodified)` rows in §1**
>   (`stable-diffusion-v1-4`, family `unclassified`, across `dreambooth` 300/600, `full_unet`

>   `full_unet`/300 at `tested 77 | gate-valid 71 | max H (valid) 1.0000`). **No other row in this
>   file inherits a duplicate-cell disagreement.** All 178 duplicate rows are
>   `admissible_for_recovery = true`, so each **double-counts** in every `tested` and `gate-valid`
>   column.
>
>   **NO FAVOURABLE DUPLICATE HAS BEEN CHOSEN.** No disagreement is adjudicated and no number is
>   changed anywhere in this file. Note the selection hazard that makes this matter: of the 13 cells
>   surviving the strictest key, 11 straddle a schema boundary and **the older stratum reports the
>   higher `H_after` in every disagreeing pair**, which `max(H_valid)` **systematically selects**.
>   Two same-stratum disagreements have **no available explanation**. Compounding it, 14 runner
>   scripts pool campaigns and take the **first glob match** then `break`, so which record lands in a
>   curve is **filesystem-order-dependent**.
> - The registry's `attack_records_quarantined: 0` is **vacuously zero** — its only glob matches
>   nothing — not a verified absence of quarantine.
> - **THE VALIDITY GATE IS NOT DEFECTIVE, and `max H (valid)` is not affected by any gate defect.**
>   `T_rise ≥ 0.20` on a 24-image panel **correctly accepts 5/24 = 0.2083 and correctly rejects
>   4/24 = 0.1667**. The rule is well-defined and was applied consistently to all 808 records; **no
>   record was mis-gated and no verdict in any row below changes.** The 13 invalid records sitting at

## 1. Per defence build x attack family x budget

`max H (valid)` is over GATE-VALID attacks only; `max H (ungated)` includes attacks whose T did not rise, which are **inconclusive, not evidence either way**.

**Three reading rules for this table, added 2026-10-26 on independent review.**

1. **The gate that produces the `gate-valid` column is correct.** `T_rise ≥ 0.20` on a 24-image panel accepts 5/24 = 0.2083 and rejects 4/24 = 0.1667. No row's gate count is affected by any gate defect, because there is none (`D-024`, withdrawn). The genuine caveat is `FINDING72`'s measured gate **bias**, non-monotone in `T_before`.
2. **`tested` and `gate-valid` are inflated wherever duplicates exist**, which within this snapshot means the **15 `BASE(unmodified)` rows and no others**. See the provenance limits above.
3. **A low `max H` in a cell with `gate-valid = 0` is not robustness evidence.** 57 of 341 cells have zero valid records and 10 of 112 arms have none at all; the gate conflates vacuous/ceiling arms with genuinely unmeasurable ones whose `T_rise` runs negative to **−0.2500**.

**Denominators, because no row states them:** H = **15** images, T = **24** images (8 prompts × 3), `legacy_retain8` = **120** images, `utility_all_nontarget` = **165**, paired panel = **48**. "retain8 (n=8)" and "all-non-target (n=11)" count **concepts, not images** — the real steps are 15× finer, and no inference below one image is supportable.

## 4. Change log — 2026-10-26 (Agent 6, provenance audit)

**No generated row was altered.** This file is machine-generated and the standing instruction is to
regenerate rather than hand-edit; that instruction was respected. Two additions were made around the
generated content:

| what | why |
|---|---|
| **A `⚠ STALE` banner at the top**, quantifying the registry/repository gap and listing the missing records and builds | the header asserted "every number below is computed from the raw records". That is true of `outputs/registry_v1.json` and **false of `outputs/`**, which has gained 150 JSON files since the registry was built — including every arm behind `FINDING71`–`FINDING78`. A reader citing these tables as a current inventory would be wrong, and `T2I_REPORT_r5.md` §2 had already transcribed the stale counts into prose |

Neither fact was documented, and neither is visible from the rows themselves |
| **This change log** | so the additions are attributable and so a regeneration run knows exactly what to drop |

  **0.1167** (§2) is the figure `FINDING78` cites for variant A's collapse.

### On regeneration

When `scripts/registry_v1.py` is next run, **delete this banner and this change log** — they
describe a gap that regeneration closes. The two provenance facts, however, are **not** fixed by
regeneration: `unet: null` and `target: null` are properties of the historical records themselves,
and the generator can only keep printing dashes for them. Making those rows attributable would
require re-deriving the checkpoints, which `T2I_REPORT_r5.md` §5 records as possible but not
weight-verifiable. Carrying the limitation forward in prose is the honest option.
